reflections.title: Running Away from the Lord

reflect.text: When God told Jonah to go preach in Nineveh, Jonah ran in the opposite direction. Disobedience is always a downward step away from close fellowship with the Lord. Just because Jonah quickly found a ship ready to set sail did not mean God approved. An easy opportunity or a smooth start never makes running away from our duty right.

Trying to run from the Lord is completely pointless because He is everywhere. Even when we wander, God is too merciful to leave us to our own ruin. He sends loving opposition into our lives to stop us and bring us back. It is far better to surrender to His will right away than to endure the pain of running.

questions: Are you treating an easy opportunity as God's approval even though it goes against what He asks?
Have you felt a loss of inner peace from holding back obedience to God?
reflections.prayer: Lord, forgive us for the times we run from Your instructions and seek our own comfort. Thank You for Your mercy that pursues us even when we wander into foolish choices. Help us yield to Your will today so we may walk in the peace of Your presence. Amen.

D3.author: Rick Warren
D3.work: What Happens When You Run from God
